newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 1996 gold output seen down to 110 T - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russian 1996 gold output seen down to 110 T - Tass.

text.p: Russian 1996 gold output is likely to fall by about 10 percent to 110 tonnes this year from 122 tonnes in 1995, Itar-Tass news agency quoted an Industry Minstry report as saying on Tuesday.
The document, drawn up for Wednesday's gold producers' meeting in Moscow, said output was falling fast due to a decline in both gold mining and refining.

Earlier this year Russian gold producers predicted a bigger fall, to 100-105 tonnes, and pinned the blame for the poor state of the gold industry on the absence of a viable precious metals market and a metal exchange in Russia.
The ministry report also noted that growing criminality in the gold sector has dealt a heavy blow to production, Tass said.
Producers have said that about five percent of all mined gold leaks to the black market, where some producers prefer to get cash at once instead of waiting for months for the government to pay.
They said the government owed about one trillion roubles to miners in September this year.
